01 / Selected work

From ambiguity to action.

Real operational challenges. Emerging product ideas. A closer look at how I approach both.

COLLINS AEROSPACE / RETURNS OPERATIONS01
$30K+BACKLOG PRODUCT VALUE
4+YEARS OF AGING RETURNS
Program management internshipImplemented

A clear owner.
A path out of the backlog.

Problem
Fire suppression products sat unmoved in a returns backlog spanning more than four years, with unclear ownership and customer instructions.
Action
I reconciled SAP and Excel records, clarified MRO/QC ownership, and coordinated with account and program managers on customer disposition.
Outcome
Helped clear a backlog totaling $30,000+ in products. The tracking and ownership process continued after my internship.
SAPExcelCross-functional execution
Inside the process

I connected physical part tags, repair orders, and SAP records to a master tracking file. A segregated shelf process assigned units a named owner; a Zero-Hour Return Review file supported weekly burndown meetings.

MRO and Quality Control handled returns. Customer account managers and program managers clarified what customers wanted done. Shared tracking helped these teams communicate and move unresolved items forward.

The $30,000+ figure describes the products in the backlog, rather than a measured cash recovery or savings figure.

NORTHROP GRUMMAN / RESOURCE PLANNING02
25ACTIVE PROJECTS
12PROJECT MANAGERS
Business management internshipAdopted by leadership

Making workload visible.
Making allocation clearer.

Problem
A growing project pipeline made it difficult to see workload imbalances and distribute assignments across project managers.
Action
I brought Tableau and SAP data into Excel, using pivot tables, charts, and workload metrics to analyze 25 projects across 12 managers.
Outcome
Presented the tool and findings to upper management, who adopted it for ongoing workload analysis and resource allocation.
Excel analyticsTableau / SAP dataDecision support
From analysis to adoption

The portfolio included many projects valued above six figures and incoming multimillion-dollar aircraft hangar work. I focused on helping leadership understand assignment distribution and manager workload.

The outcome was an adopted decision-support tool. A numerical reduction in workload imbalance or planning time has not been measured.

ADVISR / COURSE DISCOVERY03
advisr ✳Your goals → your courses
Concentration
Career fit
Eligibility
ILLUSTRATIVE PRODUCT FLOW · CONCEPT PROTOTYPE
Fundamentals of Tech PM · Team projectPrototype

Course discovery that starts
with the student.

Problem
Finding courses across NYU can mean navigating scattered listings without clear connections to a student’s interests and career goals.
Action
I contributed to a team concept and used AI-assisted coding to prototype a scheduling assistant alongside the registration workflow.
Outcome
A demonstrated concept prototype with personalized recommendations, course-fit explanations, and simulated eligibility checks.
AI-assisted prototypingProduct discoveryMVP scoping
Scope, trade-offs & next steps

The team narrowed its initial audience to Gallatin sophomores. The MVP prioritized cross-school recommendations, eligibility guidance, and career fit; adviser summaries were deferred to a later sprint.

The registration interface is a concept mockup, not an NYU product. Student records, recommendations, and registration connections are simulated. Real API access and user validation remain future dependencies.

Next validation step: test whether students act on explained recommendations before investing in a live integration.

BETA ALPHA PSI / COMMUNITY SERVICE04
Sign up→Check in / out→Credit confirmed
PROPOSED WORKFLOW · UNDER 1 MINUTE IS A TARGET
Independent product initiativeIn progress

Less time proving service.
More time doing it.

Problem
Scattered forms, sheets, and emails make attendance verification manual and leave candidates unsure whether their service credit counted.
Action
I’m surveying BAP members and developing an app around candidate check-in, committee verification, and a unified service-hour record.
Target
Make logging and verification take under one minute, with clear credit status. User research and development are ongoing.
User surveysWorkflow designRequirements definition
Designing for both sides

Candidates need quick check-in and check-out, plus confidence that their attendance counted. Committee members need one path from sign-up to attendance to points, without repeatedly copying records.

The product direction prioritizes low cost, minimal setup, and a workflow any committee member can run. The under-one-minute goal has not yet been validated; no adoption or time-savings results are claimed.

02 / About me

Grounded in operations.
Drawn to product.

I like the moment a messy process starts to make sense.

I’m a junior at NYU Stern, concentrating in AI, Computing & Data Science and Operations. My internships in aerospace and defense taught me to work through incomplete data, unclear ownership, and competing priorities.

At Collins Aerospace and Northrop Grumman, I learned how much a useful tool depends on understanding the people and decisions around it. Now I’m applying that perspective to student-facing products: an AI-assisted course discovery prototype and a simpler community service workflow.

I’m pursuing product management internships in technology and fintech, where I can bring analytical rigor, cross-functional experience, and a willingness to learn by building.
